item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01770","case1_error":"Evaluates 48 − 17 − 10 as 11 instead of 21, understating remaining stock and profit.","case2_error":"Reverses Ben's relationship to Jack, adding $9 instead of subtracting it.","reason":"Case 1 incorrectly evaluates a correct subtraction expression; case 2 constructs an incorrect relationship.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01771","case1_error":"Treats the three men's combined $150 earnings as individual earnings and multiplies by three again.","case2_error":"Provides unsupported numerical outputs ending in 1020 after correct formulas that yield 840.","reason":"Case 1 explicitly double-counts the workforce; case 2 supplies incorrect numbers without showing the calculation responsible.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01772","case1_error":"Includes a Monday count and omits Tuesday's two tile-counting rounds when forming the Tuesday total.","case2_error":"Adds only one three-second elevator stop despite the stated stop on every floor.","reason":"Case 1 uses counts from the wrong day and omits relevant counts; case 2 fails to multiply a repeated delay by its occurrences.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01773","case1_error":"Multiplies miles directly by dollars per gallon, omitting conversion from miles to gallons using fuel efficiency.","case2_error":"Treats 18 leftover watermelons as sold, then adds monetary amounts to obtain an initial watermelon count.","reason":"Case 1 omits a required unit conversion; case 2 misidentifies remaining inventory and uses an invalid money-to-inventory relationship.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01774","case1_error":"Subtracts only two duplicated movie counts, although two movies counted three times require subtracting four.","case2_error":"Evaluates 476 − 75 as 391 instead of 401.","reason":"Case 1 uses an incorrect overlap correction; case 2 numerically miscalculates a correctly written expression.","judgment":"different"}]}
